paragraphs: (Doeg the Edomite, [Psalms 52:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Psalms.52.2).) [Yoma 38b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.38b.4), also cited in [Torat Kohanim, Bechukotai](https://www.sefaria.org/Sifra%2C_Bechukotai%2C_Chapter_6.3), and [Eichah Rabbah 1:51](https://www.sefaria.org/Eikhah_Rabbah.1.51), relates that Doeg ben Yosef’s father left him a small child to his mother. Every day his mother measured him in handbreadths and gave his weight in gold to the Temple. When the enemy prevailed, his mother slaughtered and ate him.[^1]

notes.text: The Psalm names Doeg the Edomite. The narrative parallels name Doeg ben Yosef, with no identification made between the two. Both midrashic parallels give the measurement as yearly, while Yoma and Hyman say it was daily.
